html:
Olof Palme was the Social Democratic prime minister of Sweden from 1969 to 1976 and again from 1982 until he was shot dead on a Stockholm street on 28 February 1986.

He extended the welfare state and was outspoken abroad: he condemned the American war in Vietnam, apartheid in South Africa and the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia. That made him admired in the Third World and disliked by many in Washington, Moscow and at home.

He was walking home from a cinema with his wife, without bodyguards, when he was killed. The case went unsolved for decades; in 2020 prosecutors named a suspect who had died in 2000, and closed it. The murder ended a sense of Swedish innocence. See Sweden and the Cold War.
sum: Olof Palme was the Social Democratic prime minister of Sweden from 1969 to 1976 and again from 1982 until he was shot dead on a Stockholm street on 28 February 1986.
